results.title: (World Cup) S. Korea coach confident in team's preparation for tournament | Yonhap News Agency
highlights:
ZAPOPAN, Mexico, June 10 (Yonhap) -- On the eve of his team's first match at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, South Korea head coach Hong Myung-bo said Wednesday he is confident in the level of his players' preparation.
[...]
"The World Cup is a dream-come-true moment for football players. I feel like we have left no stone unturned in our preparation for this competition," Hong said at the prematch press conference at Estadio Guadalajara. "I hope that our players' sacrifices, dedication and struggles together will all pay off in tomorrow's match and will lead to a good result. Overall, I think they are in good form, and I think we're fully ready today."
[...]
At No. 25 in the latest FIFA rankings, South Korea will be favored over 41st-ranked Czechia. And Hong said there is a great deal of optimism internally about the opening match, with the starting XI also set in his mind.
[...]
"Not only is this our first match of the tournament, I believe this will be the first time we're playing on the opening day of a World Cup," Hong said. "The eyes of the world will be upon us, and I hope the players will stay composed. Though I can't reveal our plans, we will have our own set of plans to prepare for tomorrow's match."
[...]
Hong also said he was pleased with the way his players have gotten acclimated to playing in the high altitude. With two of their three Group A matches scheduled at Estadio Guadalajara, about 1,500 meters above sea level, South Korea trained in another elevated city, Salt Lake City, Utah, for about three weeks beginning in mid-May. They also played two friendly matches there.
[...]
"We began checking data on players since the start of our U.S. camp, and they had some difficulties early on," Hong said. "By now, everyone is fully acclimated. I don't know what kind of results this will bring, but I think our players will feel assured and confident that their bodies are adjusted to the thin air. I am quite satisfied with their data."
[...]
Hong said he has already spoken to players on many occasions that he may not need to deliver any special pep talk on the day of the match, though it will depend on what the vibe may be among the players.
[...]
Hong, 57, played at four World Cups and is now coaching at his second World Cup. He described his first turn on the bench, the 2014 tournament in Brazil, as a "failure," after South Korea had a draw and two losses to be eliminated in the group stage.
[...]
"I'm so honored to be here. I think I've prepared for this World Cup really well by building on my past experience," he said. "I can't predict results, but I have created an environment where the players can have fun and compete with energy. That's what's important to me, and that's a positive for the team."

results.title: 'Concerns over experimental attack lineup,' Coach Hong Myung-bo: "Tactical understanding is complete... We will focus on refining combinations" [Q&A from Guadalajara] | STARNEWS
highlights:
Under Hong Myung-bo, the South Korean national football team has finally begun its first field training in Guadalajara, Mexico, the site of the decisive matches, officially starting the countdown to the tournament.
[...]
The South Korean national football team, led by Coach Hong Myung-bo, conducted FIFA Community Training at Chivas Valle Verde, the team's base camp training ground in Guadalajara, Mexico, on the afternoon of the 6th (local time). This open training session is similar to the open training events held by the Korea Football Association in Korea and marks the first official schedule for the national team since arriving in Mexico.
[...]
Before the training, Coach Hong Myung-bo met with the press and said, "Thank you for traveling such a long distance. The team checked into their accommodation yesterday and unpacked, and we are conducting our first training today." He added, "Since this event was arranged to communicate with local Mexican fans, we plan to conduct a light training session today in line with the spirit of open training."
[...]
He continued, "The three days of training from the 7th to the 9th will likely be the most important for this tournament. While we cannot predict what results this process will ultimately yield, the players have undergone excellent training and prepared thoroughly. We will do our best to finish well during the remaining training period."
[...]
"We began a pre-camp in Salt Lake City, USA, on the 28th of last month to adapt to the high-altitude environment and adjust to the time difference. It is difficult to provide a specific numerical figure for our current preparation status. However, through the two friendly matches held in the United States, we have clearly identified the team's strengths and weaknesses. In the remaining time, the most important thing is to improve the completeness of our tactics. The same applies to managing the players' physical condition. The weather here is also different from the pre-camp location. Since there is not enough time to attempt too much at this stage, we plan to focus intensively on raising the completion level of several tactical points."
[...]
-The attacking lineup combinations have been changing continuously in recent friendly matches. There are also concerns about tactical stability.
[...]
"That is precisely why the remaining three days of training have become extremely important. Fortunately, all players now perfectly understand and have memorized the tactical model the national team intends to use on the tournament stage. Regarding the specific attacking combinations and on-field chemistry, we plan to refine them perfectly through intensive training over the next three days."

results.title: [On-site Focus] "No special delivery" Director Hong Myung-bo's confidence, "All preparations are ready"... "I can't reveal it, but I'll come forward with my own plan." < 대표팀 < 국내축구 < Football < 기사본문 - Sportal Korea
highlights:
A day before the first round, which will determine the fate of the national team, coach Hong Myung-bo appeared at an official press conference with "captain" Son Heung-min. On this day, director Hong Myung-bo exchanged questions and answers with reporters from all over the world, including the Czech Republic and Mexico, as well as Korea.
[...]
Coach Hong Myung-bo said, "The World Cup will open tomorrow. The World Cup can be said to be the stage of soccer players' dreams. There was no negligence in preparing for this tournament, he said. "In particular, I hope that the players' dedication, effort, and accumulation will be able to come to tomorrow's game and produce good results. Overall, the players are in good condition, and there are no special problems. All preparations have ended today," he said.
[...]
When asked what they would talk about in their final meeting with the team, he said, "I've played a lot of games with the players and delivered various messages. Today and tomorrow, there is no special delivery. Of course, if you wake up tomorrow, you can see and grasp the overall appearance and facial expression and talk briefly. I've already delivered all the messages, and the team understands it," he said.
[...]
The biggest concern before the game is the best 11 to play against the Czech Republic. Coach Hong Myung-bo said he had completed his plan for the match against the Czech Republic prior to the final quenching at the base camp site of Chivas Belle Verde in the afternoon of the previous day.
[...]
Coach Hong Myung-bo said, "I thought a lot about the best 11. "We have a fixed number of members tomorrow," he said, adding, "Since arriving in the United States, we have been checking the adaptation to the highlands. There were difficulties at first. There were also differences between individual players because their physical conditions were different. Now, it is in a state of perfect adaptation overall. I don't know what this will bring, but I think the players will be able to play with a sense of relief and confidence that they have adapted to the high ground. In that respect, I am very satisfied with the current data and the players' condition," he said.
[...]
Finally, questions were asked about how to play against the Czech Republic. Coach Hong Myung-bo said, "First of all, the most important thing is to see how much the players can do in the first game. Internally, it's very positive. It's the first game, and it's the game to start the World Cup. I think it's the first time in history to play on the opening day of the World Cup, but there will be a lot of attention. I want the players to play more comfortably. I can't say what I'll do strategically, but I'll play with my own plan," he stressed.
